note: Narration of The Fox and the Moon, made through the ElevenLabs claude.ai connector (eleven_v4), cap 20,000 credits. Decisions 14-16 in docs/reviews/2026-10-fable.md. Never overwrite an entry with review 'approved'.

round1.text:
Every night, a fox climbed a hill to sit beneath the moon.

He told her small things: where the blackberries grew, what he had mistaken for a bird, which paths he disliked walking alone.

The moon began waiting for him.

pick.note: The only Yes. Tom's other take (G) was a No.

round2.purpose: Decision 15 with one finalist: Tom records the first and last groups of decision 16 as production takes.

cut.tail: One evening, she asked him to meet her beside a pond.

g1.text:
Every night, a fox climbed a hill to sit beneath the moon.

He told her small things: where the blackberries grew, what he had mistaken for a bird, which paths he disliked walking alone.

The moon began waiting for him.

From so far away, each found the other easy to love.

One evening, she asked him to meet her beside a pond.

cut.head: Neither returned to the pond.
cut.tail: Every night, a fox climbed a hill to sit beneath the moon.

g6.text:
Neither returned to the pond.

Then, one evening, the fox climbed the hill with a small, unimportant story he had saved for her.

She was already looking down.

He began telling it.

Halfway through, he looked toward the pond.

The moon looked too.

Every night, a fox climbed a hill to sit beneath the moon.
